plugin_desc: SNMP monitoring template for Alcoma transmission device. It reports uptime, temperature, and interface traffic, for microwave radio and wireless transmission devices (enterprise PEN 12140).
name: Transmission

metrics.name: temperature_celsius
metrics.description: Alcoma alMP radio temperature in degrees Celsius (alMPTemperature, scalar 1.3.6.1.4.1.12140.2.3.9.0 under PEN 12140). Offline units report -1, which is dropped at collection time. High values may indicate RF hardware thermal stress, high ambient temperature or overloaded hardware.

metrics.name: rx_level_db
metrics.description: Alcoma alMP receive level in dB (alMPRX-Level, scalar 1.3.6.1.4.1.12140.2.3.4.0 under PEN 12140). Offline units report -128, which is dropped at collection time. A dropping receive level is an early sign of path fade, antenna misalignment or radio degradation.

metrics.name: tx_power_db
metrics.description: Alcoma alMP transmit power in dB (alMPTX-PWR, scalar 1.3.6.1.4.1.12140.2.3.3.0 under PEN 12140). Offline units report -128, which is dropped at collection time. Unexpectedly low transmit power can indicate radio mute, hardware fault or configuration change.

metrics.name: snr_db
metrics.description: Optional Alcoma alMP signal-to-noise ratio in dB (alMPSNR, scalar 1.3.6.1.4.1.12140.2.4.2.0 under PEN 12140). The device returns text; the first number in it is used, and empty or non-numeric text is dropped. Some firmware omits this object. A dropping SNR is an early sign of path fade or interference.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCInOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of bytes received over the past 5 minutes, based on the 64-bit ifHCInOctets counter which does not wrap on high-speed interfaces.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCOutOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of bytes sent over the past 5 minutes, based on the 64-bit ifHCOutOctets counter which does not wrap on high-speed interfaces.

metrics.name: snmp_uptime
metrics.description: This metric indicates the uptime of the device since the last restart. By monitoring the uptime, network administrators can understand the stability and reliability of the device and identify potential reboot or failure issues.
